reason: E2 confirms the initial nanocrystalline structure and Cr–V precipitation after irradiation at 1073 K, supporting premises 1 and 2. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that rapid SPS preserves nanocrystallinity or that grain boundaries suppress Cr–V precipitation in this alloy; E1 actually shows homogenization without precipitation in a related alloy, which does not directly support the proposed mechanism. The key premises about SPS and kinetic suppression are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 has a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of grains below 100 nm
Irradiation of W38Ta36Cr15V11 at 1073 K to ~8 dpa causes Cr–V precipitation
Grain boundaries can act as defect sinks that suppress diffusion-driven precipitation
Rapid SPS below 1000 K with short dwell times can preserve nanocrystalline grain structure
Preserving nanocrystallinity will kinetically suppress Cr–V precipitation under irradiation
